review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.
The Saudi supply workaround materially softens, but does not remove, the existing middle-east-oil-supply-shock thread: Brent remained near $108 while Hormuz traffic stayed severely constrained.
The Houthi F-15 claim was read in full from Business Recorder/AFP. It is conflict and shipping-risk evidence, not proof of an additional oil-facility outage.
The KSE-100 recomposition and Pakistan fuel-price stories are carried forward because they remain valid reviewed evidence; they were not reinterpreted as new stories.
Stories not reviewed are not Neutral ratings.

reviewed_stories.title: PSX recomposes KSE-100 Index, effective October 1
reviewed_stories.linkage: direct for IMAGE and THCCL; irrelevant to POWER
reviewed_stories.reason: Image Pakistan Limited and Thatta Cement Company Limited are explicitly being added to the KSE-100 from October 1, which can improve benchmark visibility and may create index-rebalancing demand. Nishat Chunian Power Limited is NCPL, not Power Cement Limited (POWER).

reviewed_stories.title: Petrol price rises Rs4.1, HSD jumps Rs6.4 from Sept 16
reviewed_stories.reason: The ex-depot petrol and HSD price increases are directly relevant to PSO's core products, but the article gives no PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital impact. A higher selling price alone is not enough to infer higher profit.

reviewed_stories.title: Saudi offers more crude via Oman loading after pipeline attacks, sources say
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration, but materially less bullish than an unresolved export-route outage
reviewed_stories.reason: Saudi Arabia is moving more crude to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, Oman, which reduces the risk that the damaged East-West pipeline and suspended Yanbu loadings translate into a prolonged loss of Saudi export volume. Brent nevertheless remained near $108 and Hormuz traffic stayed severely constrained, so the upstream price backdrop remains supportive but the supply-shock severity has eased.

reviewed_stories.title: Oil slips as Saudi Arabia offers more crude via Oman
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration; negative broad-market import and inflation backdrop
reviewed_stories.reason: Brent eased to about $107.92 as the Oman workaround reduced fears of a larger Saudi supply loss, while visible Hormuz transits remained at four versus a recent average of 18. The story changes the thread from an unmitigated export-route disruption to a partially mitigated one, but crude remains elevated enough to support upstream oil-linked exposure.

reviewed_stories.title: Yemen's Houthis say shot down Saudi fighter jet
reviewed_stories.linkage: broad-market geopolitical risk; supportive only as secondary risk-premium context for upstream oil
reviewed_stories.reason: The Houthi claim marks further military escalation and the article reiterates a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia plus attacks on Saudi ships in the Red Sea. That raises regional and shipping risk, but it does not by itself establish a new oil-facility outage or lost barrels.

IMAGE.reason: Direct company link: Image Pakistan Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, though the size of any flow is not guaranteed.

THCCL.reason: Direct company link: Thatta Cement Company Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, while the actual flow magnitude remains uncertain.

OGDC.reason: Sector continuation with mitigation: Brent remained near $108 and Hormuz traffic stayed severely constrained, but Saudi Arabia is now rerouting more crude through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman. The workaround reduces the probability of a prolonged Saudi export loss, so the upstream backdrop stays positive but with lower confidence than an unmitigated outage.

PPL.reason: Sector continuation with mitigation: crude remains elevated and regional shipping risk is high, but Saudi Arabia's Oman loading workaround reduces the risk of a prolonged loss of export barrels. That leaves PPL's upstream oil-linked backdrop positive, but less strongly than when the Saudi export-route disruption appeared unresolved.

MARI.reason: Sector continuation with mitigation: elevated crude and regional shipping risk remain supportive to upstream energy, but the Saudi Oman workaround reduces supply-shock severity. Mari's gas-heavy production mix also makes its direct crude sensitivity weaker than OGDC or PPL, so confidence is lower.

PSO.reason: Direct operating link: ex-depot petrol rose Rs4.10 per litre and HSD rose Rs6.41 effective September 16. The article does not disclose PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital effects, so the price increase is operationally relevant but not enough for a defensible positive or negative earnings call.
PSO.relevance: Direct link: core petrol and diesel products; directional earnings effect not established

Oil & Gas Exploration.reason: Brent remains near $108 and regional shipping risk is still high, but Saudi Arabia is moving more crude via Oman and Gulf loadings, reducing the risk that pipeline and Yanbu disruptions become a prolonged export-volume loss. Upstream conditions remain supportive, with lower confidence than the prior unmitigated-disruption read.
